# Independent audit: facet energy blow-up and escort recursion

Audited all six sections of
`candidate 1389446c1fac70ac`.
**PASS; no repair identified.** The exact verifier was rerun:
**271 exact checks PASS**. The analytic arguments below, not the finite
checks, establish the limit statements for arbitrary convex bodies.

## 1. Geometry and actual parameter tightness

The normal dilation has determinant `1/delta`, so its energy is exactly
`E_K(x,delta)/delta`. Compactness gives the upper convergence of the
tangential sections to the facet. The displayed homothetic copy of the
facet gives lower inclusion of every compact subset of its relative
interior, uniformly over bounded scaled-height intervals. This yields
the required almost-everywhere indicator convergence. The fixed cylinder
about `(x,1)` is valid even though its approximating section centers
move; that movement is uniformly small while their radii stay bounded
below. Dimension one reduces directly to an interval.

The fixed source ball uniformly bounds all actual minimizing parameters.
The purely normal test denominator bounds their attained energies above
by an integrable function on the fixed tangential projection times the
positive half-line. The optimal denominator floor is being applied to
each compact dilated body and is therefore legitimate.

For a convergent parameter subsequence, the floor passes to every
interior prism point and then to its closure. It excludes negative
limiting normal coefficient and guarantees a strictly positive base
denominator. A zero limiting normal coefficient would make the prism
integral infinite, contradicting the uniform energy bound by Fatou on
successively truncated prisms. Thus the limit coefficient is positive.
For a completely formal lower-limit proof, take an energy liminf
subsequence first and then its parameter-convergent subsequence; the
source's compactness/Fatou argument applies exactly to it.

## 2. Prism minimization and upper recovery sequence

Integrating out the normal variable gives the factor `1/(d b)` and the
remaining exponent `d`, exactly the energy exponent in dimension
`d-1`. Factoring out `1-b` leaves the scalar optimization of
`b(1-b)^d`. Its unique optimizer is `1/(d+1)`, giving the printed
constant `((d+1)/d)^(d+1)` and tangential minimizer
`d a_F/(d+1)`. This uses only the explicit prism integral, not an
unproved compact-body theorem on unbounded sets.

The fixed prism optimizer is indeed admissible on every sufficiently
late dilated body. At bounded heights, compactness places its tangential
points uniformly near the facet, where the base denominator has a
positive minimum. At large heights its positive normal slope dominates
all tangential terms on the bounded projection. These two ranges give
one integrable bound proportional to `(1+s)^(-d-1)`. Dominated convergence
therefore proves the upper limit. It is an actual fixed test parameter,
not an exchange of minimization with integration.

The lower and upper limits agree. Every cluster point of actual
parameters must attain the unique prism minimum, forcing convergence
of the full parameter family. Undoing the dilation gives the tangential
coefficient limit and `delta beta_delta -> 1/(d+1)` with the stated
normalization.

## 3. Derivatives and dimension one

The envelope identity is applicable at every positive `delta`, since
the marked point is interior. Its normal derivative equals
`(d+1)(E/delta)(delta beta_delta)`; its limit is exactly `C_d E_F`.
The tangential derivative divided by `delta` tends to
`d C_d E_F a_F=C_d grad E_F`, using the lower-dimensional energy
derivative exponent `d`. These are pointwise limits, not derivatives
of an unproved uniform boundary expansion.

For `d=1`, the facet is a singleton with counting measure and energy
one. The prism calculation gives constant four; the exact interval
formula `4delta(H-delta)/H` gives the same limit and normal derivative.
All tangential derivative assertions are then empty, as stated.

## 4. Escort recursion, total mass and moments

Changing variables in the original escort measure produces the scaled
density normalized by `E_(K_delta)`, since its Jacobian factor `delta`
cancels the corresponding factor in the original energy. The limiting
positive normal coefficient, bounded tangential coefficients, denominator
floor, and positive limiting energy give one common tail domination
proportional to `(1+s)^(-d-2)`. This proves L1 convergence of the densities.
Multiplying that bound by `s` remains integrable for every `d>=1`, so
normal first moments also converge; tangential coordinates are bounded.

The normal integral of the limiting density is

    [d L_F/(d+1)]^(-d-1) / [(d+1)b_* C_d E_F]
      =L_F^(-d-1)/E_F.

It is exactly the facet escort, including its correct lower-dimensional
exponent. The conditional normal mean is `A/(d b_*)=L_F`, where
`A=d L_F/(d+1)`. Its total mean is one by the facet escort identity.
For `d=1`, the limiting normal density is explicitly `2/(1+s)^3`,
whose mass and mean are both one. The bounded-tail-cutoff argument for
weak convergence in the original coordinates is valid and retains the
whole facet marginal. No boundary mass or unbounded moment is lost.

## 5. What a higher-codimension extension would actually need

The facet result has one transverse ray and one specified inward height.
For a face of dimension `k=d-r`, a proposed extension needs at least:

* the tangent-space/transverse-space decomposition and its Lebesgue
  normalization;
* the actual transverse tangent cone `C` in `R^r` along the relative
  interior of the face;
* the approach direction `eta` in the interior of that cone;
* a proved rescaled-body convergence to the corresponding product
  `F times C`, a fixed ball about the scaled marked point, and a valid
  integrable recovery denominator on the entire rescaled body.

The last items cannot be replaced by just naming the face. This audit
does not claim them for all convex faces or approach regimes.

There is an exact model computation identifying the missing transverse
constant. Suppose `C` is a closed full-dimensional POINTED convex cone,
`eta in int C`, and consider the prism `F times C` marked at `(x,eta)`.
For `b in int(C^*)`, define

    J_C(b)=int_C (1+b.t)^(-d-1) dt.

This is finite because `b.t` dominates a positive multiple of `|t|`
on `C`, and `d+1>r`. Integration after the scaling `t=A v` gives

    int_C (A+b.t)^(-d-1) dt=A^(-k-1) J_C(b).

Thus the exact infimum of positive affine-denominator integrals on this
prism is

    E_F(x) inf_{b in int C^*, 0<b.eta<1}
                  J_C(b)/(1-b.eta)^(k+1)               (13)

    =E_F(x) (d+1)^(d+1)/[r^r(k+1)^(k+1)]
          inf_{e in int C^*, e.eta=1} J_C(e).           (14)

Indeed tangential optimization gives the `k`-dimensional energy; then
write `b=q e`, use `J_C(qe)=q^(-r)J_C(e)`, and optimize
`q^r(1-q)^(k+1)` at `q=r/(d+1)`. When `k=0`, use `E_point=1`.
For `r=1`, the cone is the positive ray and `eta=1`, so `J_C(1)=1/d`
and (14) recovers the facet constant exactly.

Pointedness is material for this finite prism model. If the transverse
cone contains a line, a positive affine denominator must have zero
coefficient along that line, and the prism integral is infinite. Even
for a pointed cone, a coefficient on the dual boundary has infinite
integral: a null cone ray translates a fixed interior ball indefinitely
without changing its denominator bounds. Hence the finite model really
uses an interior dual coefficient. Curved boundary approaches with a
nonpointed tangent cone require different transverse scaling or further
local shape data; the facet proof does not settle them.

The cone dependence is visible without asymptotics of arbitrary bodies.
For `d=2`, both triangles

    conv{0,(1,0),(0,1)},
    conv{0,(1,0),(1/2,1)}

have the same zero-dimensional face `{0}`. At the marked point
`(delta,delta)`, their exact simplex energy formulas give limiting
coefficients of `E/delta^2` equal to `27/2` and `27/4`, respectively.
The direction lies inside both vertex cones. Thus face energy and
codimension alone cannot determine the answer, even for polytopes.

Equations (13)--(14) are proved calculations for the indicated infinite
prism only. They identify the additional geometric data a general
higher-codimension blow-up theorem would have to retain. They are not
being substituted for a proof of convergence from an arbitrary body,
and no mixed-integer consequence is inferred.
